home.headline: Sino-Tibetan Language Divergence Time Database
introParagraphs: The Sino-Tibetan Language Divergence Time Database aims to collect information on divergence times among languages and dialects within the Sino-Tibetan family through the historical-comparative method and lexical evidence. These lexical items carry chronological information, such as names for tool materials (stone, iron, copper), domesticated animals, introduced species or concepts, and loanwords. By combining archaeological findings and historical sources with lexical stratigraphic analysis, researchers can estimate the upper and lower bounds of divergence for target languages or dialects. Users can use this database to trace language divergence processes and compare divergence patterns across branches of the family.

The number of lexical items and languages included in this database will continue to grow as more researchers contribute. Each dataset is provided by specialists in the relevant languages and their historical development. When using materials from the database, please cite the relevant contributors and this project. The database supports search and access by language, time period, lexical item, contributor, and other criteria. Suggested citation format: contributor name, year, project title, website name, accessed on Year-Month-Date.
home.aboutPrefix: This database was designed by Dr. Hongdi Ding and Dr. Yuan Liang of the Research Centre for Chinese Language and Education, Faculty of Humanities, The Education University of Hong Kong. It is developed and maintained by independent scholars Renjun Liang and Mianyi Chen, with technical collaboration and infrastructure support from
home.aboutSuffix: including server deployment, system architecture optimization, and ongoing operations. The project brings together academic research and engineering practice, and is intended to provide linguists and historians with a professional platform for research, resource sharing, and scholarly exchange.

projects.title: Project Management
projects.description: We aim to infer the divergence times of Sino-Tibetan languages or dialects through the historical-comparative method by collecting lexical data that contain chronological information. The project also traces possible human migration routes, builds an open shared lexical database, and supports research on language evolution.

matching.question: Please evaluate the correspondence pattern for this lexical item
matching.tooltip: Complete and regular correspondence is strictly defined as systematic phonological correspondence across languages at the levels of initials, finals, and tonal systems for all syllables of a lexical item, rather than accidental surface phonetic similarity.
matching.fullNote: *Complete and regular correspondence indicates that the languages have not diverged
matching.relaxedYes: Yes. The languages with incomplete correspondence for this item occur only within the same branch of the phylogenetic tree, while complete and regular correspondence still holds across different branches
matching.relaxedNo: No. The languages with incomplete correspondence for this item occur not only within the same branch of the phylogenetic tree, but also across different branches
matching.relaxedNote: *This lexical item indicates that the languages have fully diverged
